headline: Recommended using reserves to cover the projected FY2028 deficit and set FY2029 as the target for an override.
summary: Members approved the August 12 minutes unanimously. The updated model raises the school spending cap from 3.50% to 3.75%, and school leaders raised concerns that the cap would force staff cuts. The group also discussed a $500,000 borrowing for elementary school HVAC design and the need for a full inventory of town and school needs.
decisions: Approved the August 12, 2026 meeting minutes unanimously.
Agreed that a FY2028 operational override will not be brought forward.
Recommended to the Select Board that the projected FY2028 deficit be bridged with reserves.
Agreed to target FY2029 for an override.
Agreed that a comprehensive inventory of town and school needs with approximate costs is the next deliverable.

decision_evidence.quote: On a motion by Ms. Reid-Eriksen, seconded by Mr. Matera, the Group voted unanimously to approve the minutes of the August 12, 2026 meeting.
The Group reached consensus that a proposed operational override for FY2028 will not be brought forward.

The Group reached consensus to recommend to the Select Board that the projected FY2028 deficit be bridged using one-time revenues, specifically drawdowns from the General Stabilization Fund, free cash, and other available reserve accounts.
The Group agreed to target FY2029 for an override.
The Group agreed that the next critical deliverable is a comprehensive inventory of town and school operational, maintenance, and infrastructure needs with approximate costs.
